text:
The Elias Pettersson conversation in Vancouver is now about where he plays next. NHL Trade Rumors reported this weekend that the Carolina Hurricanes have renewed their pursuit, and NHLTradeRumor.com added that the "Canucks Have an $11.6M Problem," the size of his contract. Daily Faceoff is fielding questions about whether he gets traded this year, while the team around him has lost nine of its last ten.

On the ice he's producing as a passer: 21 points in 21 games, 16 of them assists and 10 on the power play, on only 26 shots. His own chances have thinned (0.46 expected goals per 60, down from 0.74 last season), and Vancouver has scored 5.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him out there, so the points lean partly on teammates' finishing. The other end is why Canucks Army made "the case for Elias Pettersson as a Selke Trophy candidate": Vancouver's share of five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) is 6.5 points better with him on than off, and Evolving-Hockey had him facing 90th-percentile competition with bottom-5% teammates last season. His ice time is up more than two minutes a night over his last ten.
headline: Elias Pettersson, trade talk and a losing team
